requirements.title: All editing controls and creative parameters
requirements.text:
Every relevant studio should expose the parameters supported by its selected model or processing engine.

Prompt controls

Prompt, negative prompt, reference images, reference strength, subject, scene, style, composition, mood, lighting, camera angle, model, seed where supported, variation count and output constraints.

Video controls

Duration, frame size, aspect ratio, frame rate, clip range, start/end frames, motion intensity, camera motion, shot type, interpolation mode, stabilization, crop tracking, transition duration and audio behavior.

Timeline controls

Tracks, clip position, trim in/out, split, move, duplicate, ripple delete, snapping, markers, transitions, keyframes, speed, audio gain, captions, masks and track visibility.

Image-editing controls

Brush, eraser, mask, selection, crop, rotate, scale, transform, layers, opacity, blend mode, feathering, inpaint area, outpaint boundaries, background, relighting and color adjustments.

Audio controls

Track gain, fade in/out, noise reduction, speech separation, equalization, compression, loudness normalization, tempo, pitch when supported, sample rate, channels, subtitle alignment and voice settings.

Text and subtitle controls

Font, size, weight, color, outline, shadow, line spacing, word highlighting, speaker labels, position, safe margins, animation, timing, translation and export settings.

Color-grading controls

White balance, exposure, contrast, temperature, tint, saturation, vibrance, curves, levels, highlights, shadows, color wheels, LUTs, selective color, skin-tone correction and vignette.

Export controls

Format, resolution, frame rate, aspect ratio, video codec, audio codec, bitrate, quality mode, subtitle handling, filename, destination, metadata, output validation and download permissions.

requirements.title: Your own AI model families
requirements.text:
Create a dedicated Buddy Model Lab, not just a page containing a list of third-party models.

| Model family             | Intended capabilities                                       |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Buddy NLU                | Understand user requests and constraints                    |
| Buddy Planner            | Break complex requests into structured workflows            |
| Buddy Router             | Choose compatible tools and models                          |
| Buddy Vision             | Understand objects, people, scenes and composition          |
| Buddy Video Intelligence | Scene detection, temporal analysis and highlight selection  |
| Buddy Reframe            | Subject-aware crop and camera-following                     |
| Buddy Transcript         | Speech recognition and timestamp alignment                  |
| Buddy Speaker            | Diarization and speaker tracking                            |
| Buddy Localization       | Translation, subtitles and dubbing workflows                |
| Buddy Script             | Scripts, story structure and dialogue                       |
| Buddy SEO                | Metadata and channel-content optimization                   |
| Buddy Image              | Image-generation and editing model configurations           |
| Buddy Audio              | Speech enhancement and audio-understanding components       |
| Buddy Quality            | Output validation, quality assessment and regression checks |
| Buddy Evaluator          | Model comparison and benchmark execution                    |

Each entry is a model-family target; it is not evidence that a model is already trained.

### Model Lab controls

Include:

- Create model record
- Import a compatible base model
- Register a model checkpoint
- Configure a fine-tuning job
- Register a dataset
- Validate dataset licensing and consent
- Define training/validation/test splits
- Configure supported training parameters
- Estimate hardware and storage requirements
- Submit training job
- View live logs
- View actual loss and evaluation metrics
- Save checkpoints
- Compare base and fine-tuned models
- Evaluate against a fixed test set
- Register model version
- Approve a model for deployment
- Deploy to a configured endpoint
- Check endpoint health
- Compare inference latency
- Roll back a model version
- Archive or delete model artifacts
- Record provenance and licensing

Training must occur on an actual compute worker. Do not simulate training progress or invent benchmark results. Use licensed datasets and begin with practical fine-tuning or adapters before considering expensive foundation-model training.

requirements.title: All AI agents
requirements.text:
Each agent should have a defined responsibility, supported tools, permissions, execution history and evaluation criteria.

| Agent                 | Responsibility                                                 |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| AI Director           | Converts creative briefs into production plans                 |
| Research Agent        | Gathers and summarizes source-backed information               |
| Script Agent          | Develops scripts, hooks and narratives                         |
| Storyboard Agent      | Converts scripts to shot plans and panels                      |
| Video Analysis Agent  | Analyzes scenes, audio and visual content                      |
| Shorts Agent          | Finds and scores clip candidates                               |
| Reframing Agent       | Tracks subjects and selects crops                              |
| Editing Agent         | Converts editing instructions into timeline operations         |
| Image Agent           | Routes supported image-generation and editing requests         |
| Voice Agent           | Manages approved speech and voice-over tasks                   |
| Subtitle Agent        | Produces and validates subtitle files                          |
| Translation Agent     | Coordinates multilingual outputs                               |
| Music Agent           | Matches or generates suitable audio through configured engines |
| Thumbnail Agent       | Produces thumbnail concepts and variations                     |
| SEO Agent             | Creates metadata and content-optimization recommendations      |
| Trend Agent           | Analyzes trends from accessible data sources                   |
| Analytics Agent       | Interprets genuine connected-channel metrics                   |
| Publishing Agent      | Prepares or publishes content through authorized integrations  |
| Quality-Control Agent | Validates media and detects production failures                |
| Model-Selection Agent | Selects compatible models based on constraints                 |
| Cost-Control Agent    | Checks resource requirements before jobs run                   |
| Workflow Orchestrator | Coordinates agent execution and dependencies                   |

Every agent should support an appropriate subset of these controls: enable/disable, execution mode, access scope, allowed tools, model selection, resource limits, retry policy, approval requirements, logs and audit history.

Do not give agents unrestricted access to arbitrary files, secrets, user accounts or shell commands.

requirements.title: Video editor: everything it should contain
requirements.text:
The editor should be a genuine production workspace.

Workspace layout: media bin, preview monitor, timeline, tracks, inspector, effects panel, properties panel, audio mixer, captions panel, marker list and export settings.

Timeline operations: import, drag-and-drop, trim, split, ripple delete, move, duplicate, reorder, snap, zoom, markers, track locking, track muting, track visibility, undo, redo, copy, paste and supported keyboard shortcuts.

AI editing operations: natural-language edits, scene suggestions, highlight candidates, speaker tracking, smart reframing, silence removal, subtitle generation, audio cleanup, automatic pacing and suggested transitions.

Visual controls: crop, position, scale, rotation, masks, transparency, blend modes, keyframes, color correction, LUT application, blur, sharpen, denoise, stabilization and supported visual effects.

Audio operations: track gain, fade, trimming, synchronization, noise reduction, music replacement, voice-over placement and loudness normalization.

Text operations: titles, captions, animated text, lower thirds, subtitles, safe areas, font and outline styling, word highlighting and timing correction.

Export: select output range, aspect ratio, resolution, codec, bitrate, frame rate, audio settings, filename, subtitle handling and destination. Verify the completed file before showing the download action.

A tool that edits a video must modify the timeline or output file, not just generate a text recommendation.

requirements.title: Image editor: everything it should contain
requirements.text:
Canvas: zoom, pan, crop, rotate, resize, alignment, guides, grids and canvas expansion.

Layers: create, rename, duplicate, reorder, group, hide, lock, opacity, blend modes, masks and layer transformations.

Selections: rectangle, ellipse, lasso, color selection, subject selection, background selection, feathering and inversion.

Retouching: remove objects, remove backgrounds, replace objects, fill masked areas, restore damaged areas, correct perspective and adjust lighting.

AI operations: prompt-based editing, outpainting, inpainting, reference-based generation, style transfer where supported, image restoration and variations.

Color: exposure, contrast, saturation, hue, temperature, tint, curves, levels, color balance, selective color, blur and sharpening.

Export: PNG, JPEG, WebP, supported transparent images, quality settings, dimensions, compression and metadata handling.

requirements.title: Workflow canvas
requirements.text:
The workflow builder should allow users to connect tools into reusable pipelines.

Example workflow:

`Upload video → Transcribe → Detect scenes → Find highlights → Review clips → Reframe → Remove silence → Generate subtitles → Render → Validate → Export`

Workflow capabilities should include:

- Drag-and-drop nodes.
- Typed input and output ports.
- Conditional branches.
- Parallel branches where safe.
- Dependency validation.
- Per-step model selection.
- Data mapping between steps.
- User approval nodes.
- Retry policies.
- Error branches.
- Cancellation.
- Saved templates.
- Version history.
- Execution logs.
- Real-time job statuses.
- Resource estimates.
- Output validation.
- Reusable sub-workflows.

A workflow should be persisted so it can be resumed or investigated after an application or worker restart.

requirements.title: Cloud administration and operational dashboard
requirements.text:
The administration area should show actual infrastructure data:

Compute: worker availability, CPU, memory, GPU, VRAM and active processes where permitted.

Queues: queued jobs, running jobs, failures, retry counts and queue age.

Model services: active model versions, endpoint health, inference latency and error rate.

Storage: used storage, quotas, artifact counts, retention and cleanup failures.

Database: connection health, migration version, backup status and error alerts.

Provider services: configuration status, rate limits, health checks and availability.

Costs: measured usage, budget thresholds, estimated costs where reliable and actual billed costs when available from the provider.

Security: failed logins, permission denials, revoked keys, audit events, suspicious requests and dependency alerts.

Never show a universal green “All systems operational” state simply because the frontend loaded.

requirements.title: What makes the platform genuinely intelligent?
requirements.text:
The natural-language command interface should let a user ask for a finished deliverable in ordinary language.

For example:

> "Use this uploaded Telugu podcast. Find four strong moments, create 9:16 Shorts, track the active speaker, remove long silences, create Telugu captions, make English subtitle versions, generate three thumbnail options, and prepare the files for review."

The AI should then:

1. Understand the instructions and constraints.
2. Identify the correct source file.
3. Construct a structured workflow.
4. Select compatible models and processing tools.
5. Ask for approval when necessary.
6. Execute the real jobs.
7. Report actual job progress.
8. Validate the produced files.
9. Present outputs with clear names and downloadable links.
10. Explain any failed or unavailable step.

The user's request—not a hardcoded example—must drive the workflow.
